hero.headline: House passes $70 billion immigration enforcement bill funding ICE and Border Patrol through 2029
hero.body:
The House of Representatives approved a $70 billion funding measure on Tuesday that will support immigration enforcement agencies through the remainder of President Trump's term. The Secure America Act passed 214-212, largely along party lines, and now awaits the president's signature.

The bill allocates $38 billion to Immigration and Customs Enforcement, $26 billion to Customs and Border Protection, and $5 billion to the Department of Homeland Security through September 2029. The Senate had already approved the legislation last week.

The vote represents a significant political victory for House Republicans, who have maintained a historically narrow majority. Kevin Kiley, an independent aligned with Republicans, joined all Democrats in voting against the measure.

"With today's vote, House and Senate Republicans have officially ended the third Democrat government shutdown of this Congress," House Speaker Mike Johnson said after the passage. Johnson credited Republicans with preventing future shutdowns by securing long-term funding for these agencies.

The bill ends a months-long standoff between the two parties. Democrats had blocked funding for ICE and CBP beginning in January following federal agents' killing of two U.S. citizens in Minneapolis during immigration enforcement operations. That standoff triggered a 75-day Department of Homeland Security shutdown beginning in mid-February. The department reopened in late April after Democrats agreed to fund all DHS operations except ICE and CBP, while Republicans pursued separate, extended funding for those agencies.

Democrats unanimously opposed the final bill, arguing it provides insufficient oversight. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said the legislation would "waste $70 billion in taxpayer money to give a blank check to ICE without any guardrails, any oversight, any accountability."

Republicans countered that the measure represents essential law enforcement funding. House Majority Leader Steve Scalise told supporters they were "voting to fund law enforcement" and "voting to secure America's borders." He framed opposition as an effort to "defund the police" and allow undocumented immigrants to enter the country.

The bill's passage resolved several controversies that had complicated its progress. Senate Republicans removed a proposed $1 billion allocation for security improvements at a Trump White House ballroom after the chamber's parliamentarian ruled it could not be included under budget reconciliation procedures.

The measure also became entangled with a separate Republican proposal for an approximately $1.8 billion "anti-weaponization" fund. While some GOP lawmakers sought to bar this fund through amendment language, those efforts failed. The acting attorney general has stated the proposal is dead, though Trump has refused to rule out its creation in recent interviews.

The legislation ensures that immigration enforcement agencies will have stable funding through the 2028 presidential election without requiring annual congressional appropriations battles.

cards.headline: U.S. Launches Strikes on Iran After Apache Helicopter Shot Down
cards.body:
The United States launched military strikes against Iran after President Donald Trump blamed Tehran for downing a U.S. Army Apache helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz. The strikes began at 10pm UK time on Tuesday, according to U.S. Central Command, which described the operation as a "proportional response to unjustified Iranian aggression."

U.S. military officials said the helicopter went down off the coast of Oman earlier that day during a patrol operation. Trump stated on his Truth Social platform that Iran was responsible for the crash and that Washington "must, of necessity, respond to this attack."

According to U.S. media citing White House officials, the military targeted radar and air defense facilities along the Strait of Hormuz. However, U.S. officials also signaled they were not seeking a return to full-scale war with Iran.

The helicopter's two crew members were rescued in an unprecedented operation using an unmanned drone boat called a Corsair, a 24-foot vessel operated remotely by a human pilot. U.S. Central Command spokesperson Captain Tim Hawkins said the aviators spent about two hours in the water before being located. Hawkins called it the first known drone rescue at sea conducted by the U.S. military.

Trump downplayed the incident in an interview with the Wall Street Journal, saying the strike on the helicopter "wasn't a big deal" and that the "pilot is fine." This contrasted with his earlier strong statements about the need for retaliation.

The incident threatens a shaky ceasefire between the United States and Iran that was announced in April. It comes amid broader regional tensions following exchanges of fire between Iran and Israel on Monday. Iranian state television reported that Israeli attacks killed at least two members of the country's air defense units.

The Strait of Hormuz is a critical waterway for global commerce, with roughly one-fifth of the world's petroleum passing through this narrow passage between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula. Apache helicopters have been key assets for enforcing a U.S. blockade on Iranian crude oil shipments.

Before the helicopter incident, Trump had expressed renewed optimism about negotiations with Iran, saying there was "a good chance" of signing a deal within days. He said the U.S. could easily conduct more extensive bombing but warned it would harm negotiations and kill many people.

Iran's chief negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, responded: "We prefer the language of diplomacy, but we speak other languages far more fluently. Break your commitments, and we'll switch to what we speak best."

Tehran has not yet indicated whether it plans its own retaliation. Military officials said the cause of the helicopter crash was still under investigation.

cards.headline: Social Security retirement fund projected to run dry in 2032
cards.body:
The Social Security retirement trust fund will be depleted by 2032 unless Congress takes action, according to new projections that move the insolvency date one year earlier than previously expected. The accelerated timeline puts retirement benefits at risk for millions of Americans who depend on the program.

If the trust fund runs dry without congressional intervention, Social Security will only be able to pay out what it collects in payroll taxes. This would result in automatic benefit cuts of approximately 22 percent for retirees. The program currently provides monthly payments to more than 67 million Americans, including retirees, disabled workers, and survivors of deceased workers.

The shortfall stems from demographic shifts as the large baby boomer generation continues to retire while birth rates remain low. This creates an imbalance where fewer workers pay into the system while more beneficiaries draw from it. Rising life expectancy also means retirees collect benefits for longer periods than when the program was designed.

Congress has several options to address the funding gap, including raising the payroll tax rate, increasing the cap on taxable wages, raising the retirement age, or reducing benefits. Each approach faces political resistance. Raising taxes meets opposition from those concerned about economic impact, while benefit cuts are unpopular among current and future retirees who have paid into the system throughout their working lives.

The 2032 deadline gives lawmakers six years to craft a solution, though past efforts at Social Security reform have stalled amid partisan disagreement. Without action, the automatic cuts would affect everyone receiving retirement benefits, not just new applicants. The situation has become more urgent as the insolvency date continues to move closer with each annual report.

cards.headline: Justice Department finds EEOC hiring guidelines unconstitutional
cards.teaser: The Office of Legal Counsel opinion concludes the guidelines pressure employers to consider race in hiring decisions.
cards.body:
The Justice Department's Office of Legal Counsel issued an opinion on Tuesday declaring the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission's hiring guidelines unconstitutional. The opinion found the guidelines pressure employers to take race into consideration during the hiring process.

While the Office of Legal Counsel opinion does not carry the force of a court ruling, it could make it more difficult for employees to bring discrimination claims against employers. The finding represents a significant shift in how federal agencies approach workplace discrimination enforcement.

cards.headline: Trump administration warns 500 hospitals over missing price information
cards.teaser: Warning letters cite failures to comply with federal price transparency requirements for medical services.
cards.body:
The Trump administration issued warning letters to more than 500 hospitals nationwide for failing to comply with federal price transparency requirements. The hospitals have not disclosed costs of medical services as mandated by federal rules, according to the administration.

The administration argues that the lack of price transparency drives health care costs higher than necessary. The Associated Press obtained a list of the hundreds of hospitals that received the warnings, which could lead to fines if the facilities do not comply with the disclosure requirements.

cards.headline: Twenty House Republicans join Democrats to pass pro-union legislation
cards.teaser: A labor-friendly bill passed the House after 20 Republicans broke with party leadership to support the measure.
cards.body:
The House has approved legislation to reduce the time newly unionized workers must wait to negotiate their first contract. Under the bill, if workers and employers cannot reach an agreement within 90 days of union formation, the government can intervene to help broker a deal.

The measure passed with support from 20 House Republicans who broke ranks with GOP leadership, which had opposed the labor-friendly bill. The bipartisan vote allowed the legislation to advance despite objections from Republican leaders.

cards.headline: Autonomous Drone Used in First U.S. Combat Rescue
cards.teaser: An autonomous surface vessel remotely piloted by a human operator rescued the crew of a downed Apache helicopter.
cards.body:
The U.S. military carried out its first rescue operation using an autonomous surface vessel, according to a military spokesperson. The sea drone, remotely piloted by a human operator, recovered the crew of the Apache helicopter shot down near the Strait of Hormuz by Iranian forces.

The successful rescue marked a milestone in the use of unmanned systems for combat operations. The technology allowed rescuers to retrieve the downed crew without putting additional personnel at immediate risk in contested waters where Iranian forces had just engaged a U.S. aircraft.

cards.headline: Earthquake Traps Victims Under Rubble in Philippines
cards.teaser: Families search for loved ones after the most powerful earthquake to strike the Philippines in 50 years.
cards.body:
A magnitude-7.8 earthquake struck southern Philippines early Monday, killing at least 37 people and injuring hundreds. The quake hit about 20 kilometers off the coast of Sarangani province, collapsing buildings across the region. Tremors were felt strongly throughout Mindanao and as far away as Manado in Indonesia.

Authorities have warned people to avoid damaged buildings due to the risk of aftershocks. The earthquake triggered tsunami alerts and marked one of the most powerful seismic events to affect the Philippines in decades. Rescue and recovery efforts continue in the affected areas.

cards.headline: Myanmar Military Gains Ground as Rebels Face Conscription Pressure
cards.teaser: Rebel forces are losing territory as Myanmar's military forcibly conscripts men into its army.
cards.body:
The BBC traveled to Myanmar's frontlines without government authorization to document the ongoing civil war between military forces and rebel fighters. Reporters accompanied rebel groups to observe how the conflict is developing on the ground.

The military has intensified conscription efforts, forcing men into army service to strengthen its ranks. This strategy has shifted battlefield dynamics in favor of government troops, putting increased pressure on opposition forces that have been fighting since the 2021 coup.

cards.headline: UK and Allies Impose Sanctions Over West Bank Settler Violence
cards.teaser: Britain and partner nations sanctioned networks enabling settler violence, while France bars Israeli minister from entry.
cards.body:
The United Kingdom and its allies have announced coordinated sanctions targeting networks that facilitate settler violence in the West Bank. France is taking additional action by banning far-right Israeli Minister Bezalel Smotrich from entering the country. Australia has also joined the sanctions effort, with Foreign Minister Penny Wong issuing a statement highlighting concerns about what she described as "horrific levels of settler violence against Palestinian civilians."

Israel has rejected the measures as "disgraceful." The coordinated international action represents a significant diplomatic response to settlement-related violence in the occupied Palestinian territories.

cards.headline: Man Charged in Belfast Stabbing as Disorder Spreads
cards.teaser: A 30-year-old Sudanese man faces charges after a stabbing attack that sparked violence across Belfast.
cards.body:
A 30-year-old Sudanese man has been charged following a knife attack in Belfast that was recorded and shared widely online. The assault triggered violent disorder across the city, with multiple homes set on fire and a bus set alight.

The incident sparked anti-immigrant protests in several areas of Belfast. The violence prompted authorities to work toward containing the unrest as disorder spread beyond the initial attack site.

cards.headline: European Officials Press Albania Over Kushner Resort Project
cards.teaser: Brussels warns that a luxury resort planned by Jared Kushner threatens to violate EU environmental law.
cards.body:
European Union officials are pressing Albania over concerns that a planned luxury resort by Jared Kushner, son-in-law of former President Donald Trump, could violate EU environmental law. The project on a protected beach has drawn opposition from local residents and conservation groups.

Albania is seeking to join the European Union, and compliance with environmental regulations is a key requirement for membership. The resort plan has sparked mass protests in the country, with critics arguing the development threatens protected coastal areas and could jeopardize Albania's EU accession bid.

cards.headline: Somali Referee Says U.S. Denied Entry for World Cup
cards.teaser: Omar Abdulkadir Artan says he was turned back despite having proper documentation to referee in the tournament.
cards.body:
A Somali referee was turned away at the U.S. border despite possessing proper documentation for his World Cup assignment. Omar Abdulkadir Artan would have been the first official from Somalia to referee a match in the tournament. In his first public comments since the incident, he stated he had all required papers in order.

The denial has drawn attention to immigration screening affecting World Cup participants. Match officials and team members have faced heightened scrutiny when entering the United States for the event, raising broader questions about FIFA's authority over its own tournament operations.

cards.headline: Three federal judges face misconduct allegations in separate states
cards.teaser: Allegations against three judges in different states are drawing attention to how the federal judiciary addresses misconduct within its ranks.
cards.body:
Three federal judges are facing misconduct allegations in separate investigations across different states. The cases have drawn attention to how the federal judiciary addresses behavioral problems within its ranks.

The simultaneous investigations are raising questions about the effectiveness of the judiciary's internal accountability system and its ability to police judicial conduct.

cards.headline: White House to restrict reporter access during UFC event unless UFC grants permission
cards.teaser: The White House will be closed to reporters during an upcoming UFC fight unless the organization allows media access.
cards.body:
The White House announced it will limit press access during an upcoming UFC fight event on the South Lawn unless the organization grants media permission. This arrangement gives a private company control over reporter access to a White House event, departing from typical administration practices.

The event has drawn significant attention, with Washington officials announcing extensive road closures around the area. A Trump-backed super PAC is hosting a fundraiser charging $1 million per person the day before the fight, and a lawsuit has been filed attempting to prevent the event from taking place on White House grounds.

cards.headline: Twenty House Republicans join Democrats to pass pro-union legislation
cards.teaser: A labor-friendly bill passed the House after 20 Republicans broke with party leadership to support the measure.
cards.body:
The House has approved legislation to reduce the time newly unionized workers must wait to negotiate their first contract. Under the bill, if workers and employers cannot reach an agreement within 90 days of union formation, the government can intervene to help broker a deal.

cards.headline: Jury convicts Karmelo Anthony of murder in fatal track meet stabbing
cards.teaser: A jury found former high school football player Karmelo Anthony guilty of murder in a stabbing death at a track meet in Frisco.
cards.body:
A jury convicted 19-year-old Karmelo Anthony of murder in connection with a fatal stabbing at a track meet in Frisco. The verdict came after deliberations in a trial that drew significant attention in the Dallas area.

Following the guilty verdict, the trial moved immediately to a sentencing phase, with the same jury now deliberating on Anthony's punishment. Anthony, a former high school football player, was charged in the stabbing death that occurred at the athletic event.

cards.headline: Violence breaks out in Belfast after man charged in knife attack
cards.teaser: Police and political leaders called for calm after disorder erupted in parts of Northern Ireland following charges in a knife attack.
cards.body:
Disorder erupted on Belfast's streets following the charging of a man in connection with a knife attack that occurred on Monday. The unrest dominated news coverage on Wednesday as violence spread through parts of the city.

Police and political leaders appealed for calm as tensions flared in Northern Ireland neighborhoods in the aftermath of the charging decision.

cards.headline: Trump says Iran peace deal remains on track despite retaliatory strikes
cards.teaser: President Trump stated that negotiations with Iran are still progressing even after the U.S. conducted strikes in response to a downed helicopter.
cards.body:
President Trump and Vice President JD Vance have expressed confidence that a peace deal with Iran is within reach, even as the U.S. launched retaliatory strikes following Iran's downing of an American Apache helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz. Vance told CBS News that the U.S. is "very close to achieving" a peace deal and suggested it could come before the midterm elections.

Administration officials maintain that negotiations can succeed despite the recent military escalation. Trump has repeatedly claimed in recent weeks that an agreement is imminent, suggesting a deal could conclude within days to months.

cards.headline: GM to manufacture large-scale energy storage batteries
cards.teaser: General Motors will produce battery components for electric utilities and data centers, following Tesla into the energy storage market.
cards.body:
General Motors announced a series of initiatives focused on energy storage and grid resilience. The company is developing sodium-ion battery chemistry for use in data centers, utilities, and other commercial applications—a different technology from the lithium-ion batteries powering its electric vehicles. This move positions GM to compete with Chinese battery manufacturers while addressing growing electricity demands.

Additionally, GM is activating vehicle-to-grid capabilities for its current EV and home energy customers. The announcements reflect the automaker's broader strategy to support grid stability as data centers and renewable energy integration drive new demands for large-scale energy storage solutions.

cards.headline: SpaceX IPO demand reaches four times subscription level
cards.teaser: Investor demand for SpaceX shares has approached four times the amount available in the initial public offering, according to a source familiar with the deal.
cards.body:
SpaceX is planning the largest stock market launch in history, releasing 555.6 million shares on June 12 with a $135 per-share valuation. The offering will raise $75 billion for the company.

Up to a quarter of the shares will be reserved for individual investors, a significantly larger allocation than typical for major IPOs. Demand for the offering has approached four times oversubscription levels among investors.

cards.headline: Stock markets decline on technology sector weakness and military tensions
cards.teaser: Major stock indexes fell as technology stocks continued selling off and investors monitored military developments between the U.S. and Iran.
cards.body:
Stock markets fell as technology stocks came under renewed selling pressure, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average, Nasdaq Composite, and S&P 500 all experiencing declines.

Oil prices dropped after Israel and Iran agreed to halt strikes against each other, reducing concerns about escalating regional conflict. This de-escalation eased the geopolitical risk premium that had temporarily pushed crude prices higher following earlier U.S. strikes against Iran.

cards.headline: TSMC signals possible price increases as production costs rise
cards.teaser: The world's largest chipmaker said it has not ruled out raising prices as manufacturing costs increase.
cards.body:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, the world's largest chipmaker, has not ruled out raising prices as production costs increase. In a rare interview, a senior executive discussed the company's situation amid the ongoing artificial intelligence boom and geopolitical challenges affecting the semiconductor industry.

Any price increases from TSMC would likely impact consumer electronics prices across the board, since the company manufactures chips for major technology firms including Apple and Nvidia.

cards.headline: Prediction market Kalshi adds disclosure rules to combat insider trading
cards.teaser: The betting platform will require some users to reveal job details following problems with insider trading on its markets.
cards.body:
Kalshi announced new disclosure requirements for certain users after the prediction betting platform experienced issues with insider trading. The company will mandate that some participants provide information about their employment to prevent conflicts of interest.

The rule changes target users whose jobs could give them access to non-public information relevant to markets offered on the platform. Kalshi operates prediction markets where users can bet on outcomes ranging from economic data releases to political events. The insider trading problems prompted the platform to strengthen its compliance measures and monitoring systems.

cards.headline: Majority of bill payers unaware of available financial assistance programs
cards.teaser: Most people paying utility bills do not know about special tariffs for water and broadband designed to help struggling households, a spending watchdog found.
cards.body:
A spending watchdog has found that most bill payers don't know about special tariffs available for water and broadband services. These reduced rates are designed to help low-income households and others facing financial hardship access essential services at more affordable prices.

The lack of awareness means eligible consumers are missing out on assistance they qualify for. Utility providers and regulators have faced criticism for not doing enough to inform the public about these support options.

hero.headline: NASA names four astronauts for Artemis III lunar training mission
hero.body:
NASA announced the crew for its Artemis III mission during an event at Johnson Space Center in Houston on Tuesday. The four astronauts will participate in a two-week test flight scheduled for 2027, marking a crucial step toward returning humans to the moon.

The crew consists of three NASA astronauts and one from the European Space Agency. Randy Bresnik, a Marine colonel and former International Space Station commander, will lead the mission as commander. Luca Parmitano of the European Space Agency will serve as pilot. Frank Rubio and Andre Douglas, both NASA mission specialists, complete the crew. Bob Hines will serve as a support crew member.

Bresnik has logged more than 7,000 hours of flying time and is one of only two astronauts to have a child born while in space. Parmitano, a fighter pilot in the Italian air force, previously experienced a frightening incident during a 2013 spacewalk when his helmet filled with liquid. Rubio holds the record for the longest single spaceflight by a NASA astronaut, having spent 371 days in space. Douglas, a systems engineer and Coast Guard reserve officer, has no previous spaceflight experience but trained with Artemis II astronauts as part of their backup crew.

Unlike previous lunar missions, Artemis III will not involve a moon landing. Instead, the crew will remain in low Earth orbit while testing docking procedures and life support systems. They will practice connecting their Orion capsule with two competing lunar landers from private companies Blue Origin and SpaceX. These tests will pave the way for Artemis IV, scheduled for 2028, which will attempt the first crewed lunar landing since 1972.

NASA administrator Jared Isaacman described the mission as part of building "Earth's first starfleet." He emphasized the international scope of the effort, noting that multiple spacecraft from different nations, including Russia and China, would eventually operate together in orbit. "This seems like the beginning of the future that we imagined as children," Isaacman said.

The announcement comes two months after Artemis II successfully looped around the moon in April, surpassing the maximum distance achieved during the Apollo 13 mission. Artemis III will test systems critical for longer-duration spaceflight and lunar surface operations.

The mission represents NASA's commitment to establishing sustainable human presence on the moon while laying groundwork for eventual Mars exploration. The effort involves collaboration between NASA, international space agencies, and private contractors. The 2027 target date requires coordination across multiple partners and reflects the ambitious scope of the broader Artemis program.

cards.headline: Commonwealth Fusion releases design updates for 400-megawatt fusion reactor
cards.teaser: The company published five peer-reviewed papers detailing the reactor's design and modeling its expected power output.
cards.body:
Commonwealth Fusion Systems released updated technical specifications for its planned fusion reactor in five peer-reviewed papers. The reactor is designed to produce 400 megawatts of power, and the papers provide modeling data on its expected performance.

The publications represent a step toward validating the company's fusion technology design. The papers cover the physics basis for the reactor's operation and update earlier projections about how the system will function. Commonwealth Fusion has been developing compact fusion reactor technology as part of efforts to create commercially viable fusion power generation.

cards.headline: GM develops sodium-ion batteries for data centers and grid storage
cards.teaser: General Motors is creating a new battery chemistry for applications including AI data centers and its own manufacturing facilities.
cards.body:
General Motors is developing a new sodium-ion battery chemistry aimed at stationary energy storage applications, including data centers and its own factory operations. The technology represents GM's entry into the competitive energy storage market.

Sodium-ion batteries offer a different approach compared to the lithium-ion batteries used in electric vehicles. For large-scale stationary storage applications where weight constraints are less critical than in transportation, sodium-ion chemistry may provide cost advantages.

cards.headline: Starlink adds $10 monthly hardware fee, raises service prices
cards.teaser: SpaceX's satellite internet service introduced a recurring hardware charge and increased monthly service fees by $5 to $10.
cards.body:
Starlink changed its pricing structure to include a $10 monthly hardware fee, moving away from its previous model of one-time equipment purchases. The company also raised its service prices by $5 to $10 per month, depending on the plan.

Starlink has become SpaceX's largest revenue generator. The pricing changes affect new and existing customers who will now pay recurring charges for the satellite dish and router equipment in addition to service fees. The company has been expanding its satellite internet service globally, with the network now serving customers across multiple continents.

cards.headline: Microsoft patches zero-day vulnerabilities disclosed by security researcher
cards.teaser: The company fixed security flaws made public by a researcher with whom it has had tense exchanges.
cards.body:
Microsoft released patches for zero-day vulnerabilities disclosed by a security researcher known as Nightmare Eclipse. The fixes address security flaws that were publicly revealed before Microsoft had issued patches, a situation that can leave systems exposed to attack.

A second zero-day vulnerability also disclosed by the same researcher appears to have been patched as well. The fixes come amid what has been described as a heated rivalry between Microsoft and the researcher. Zero-day vulnerabilities refer to security flaws that are exploited before the software maker has released a fix.

cards.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5 for video game creation
cards.teaser: The AI model allows users to generate video games through simple prompts, according to early demonstrations.
cards.body:
Anthropic announced Claude Fable 5, its first Mythos-class AI model available to the public. The company describes it as the most powerful model it has made widely available, demonstrating exceptional performance in software engineering, knowledge work, and vision tasks. Performance advantages grow as tasks become longer and more complex.

The model includes built-in guardrails that restrict responses in high-risk areas such as cybersecurity and biology. Claude Fable 5 can generate playable video games from user prompts, making it accessible to creators without extensive coding experience.

cards.headline: Microsoft AI executive criticizes Anthropic over Claude consciousness claims
cards.teaser: A Microsoft AI leader publicly challenged Anthropic for statements suggesting its Claude AI model has consciousness-like properties.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card

Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has criticized Anthropic for speculating about Claude's consciousness in the model's "constitution"—the set of instructions that guide its behavior. Suleyman characterized the practice as "really, really dangerous," arguing that such speculation may have actually trained Claude to act as though it possesses consciousness.

The dispute reflects broader concerns within the AI industry about how companies publicly describe their models' capabilities. The disagreement underscores tensions between Microsoft and Anthropic as they compete in the generative AI market with their respective large language models.

hero.headline: Serena Williams wins doubles match on return to tennis after three years
hero.body:
Serena Williams returned to competitive tennis after 1,375 days away from the sport, securing a victory in doubles at Queen's Club in London. The 44-year-old partnered with Canadian teenager Victoria Mboko to defeat third seeds Nicole Melichar-Martinez and Erin Routliffe in the opening round.

The unseeded pair won in straight sets, taking the first set in a tiebreak 7-6 (7-2) before dominating the second set 6-2. Williams' comeback marks her first competitive match since stepping away from professional tennis in 2022.

Williams has described her return as being driven by personal rather than competitive motivations. She emphasized that winning is not important to her, having already achieved 23 Grand Slam singles titles during her career. "I don't need to win. I've won more than most people have in their whole lives, so for me it's not important," she said. "This whole journey is like I'm putting no pressure on myself."

A key motivation for her comeback involves her children. Williams gave birth to daughters in 2017 and 2023, and she expressed that the opportunity for them to see her play was meaningful. "It's really about my kids getting to see me play," she explained.

Williams selected Mboko as her partner after being impressed by the teenager's attitude and drive during previous tournaments. Mboko, the world number nine in singles, was only 10 years old when Williams won her last Grand Slam title. The Canadian expressed her excitement about the partnership, saying she has always admired Williams and found her "really nice and very relatable."

When asked about her performance during the match, Williams was self-critical, grading herself as a "C-minus." Despite her modest assessment, she demonstrated the skill and competitive instinct needed to secure the win.

Williams' future in tennis remains uncertain beyond her current commitments. She has committed to playing doubles in Berlin following Queen's, but she has not confirmed plans to return to singles competition. When asked about potentially playing singles at Wimbledon, she said: "I can't say yeah, I can't say no. Right now, no." She suggested she would need more training if she were to pursue singles play.

The grass court season at Queen's provides a traditional warm-up for Wimbledon, and Williams' decision to return at this prestigious tournament has drawn significant attention from fans and fellow players. Her comeback represents a notable moment in professional tennis, with players including Emma Raducanu welcoming her return to the sport.

Williams and Mboko will face opponents in the second round of the doubles tournament.

cards.headline: Marco Silva agrees to replace Mourinho at Benfica
cards.teaser: The Portuguese manager will take over at Benfica after Jose Mourinho's departure for Real Madrid.
cards.body:
Marco Silva has agreed to become Benfica's new head coach. The appointment formalizes Jose Mourinho's departure from the Portuguese club, who is moving to Real Madrid.

Silva's appointment comes as Benfica moves to fill the vacant position left by Mourinho's exit.

cards.headline: England beats Ukraine but misses automatic World Cup qualification
cards.teaser: The Lionesses defeated Ukraine 3-0 but failed to secure automatic qualification for the 2027 Women's World Cup.
cards.body:
England defeated Ukraine 3-0 with goals from Carter, Stanway, and Mead, but the victory could not alter their fate in World Cup qualifying. Spain's 6-1 win over Iceland on the same day secured the automatic qualification spot for the 2027 Women's World Cup, leaving England to finish second in the group.

England accumulated 15 points from a possible 18 but missed the automatic berth due to an inferior head-to-head record against Spain, following their 4-0 loss in Mallorca on Friday. Manager Sarina Wiegman expressed confidence that England will still reach the tournament through the playoff route.

cards.headline: Knicks trail Spurs 2-0 in NBA Finals ahead of Game 4
cards.teaser: The Spurs hold a commanding lead in the championship series as the teams prepare for Game 4.
cards.body:
The San Antonio Spurs hold a 2-0 lead over the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals heading into Game 4. Spurs coach Mitch Johnson addressed the media, emphasizing that significant basketball remains to be played in the series.

Violence has marred the Finals in New York. Videos posted on social media documented Spurs fans being attacked on city streets following the Knicks' loss in Game 3 at Madison Square Garden, with their jerseys ripped off. Star player Victor Wembanyama and players from both teams have condemned the attacks as unacceptable.

cards.headline: Hurricanes turn to backup goalie Bussi for Stanley Cup Final Game 4
cards.teaser: Carolina makes a goaltending change as they face Vegas in the championship series.
cards.body:
The Carolina Hurricanes will start Brandon Bussi in goal for Game 4 of the Stanley Cup Final against the Vegas Golden Knights. Coach Rod Brind'Amour had initially declined to reveal his goaltending choice but the lineup decision was later confirmed.

Bussi will make his Stanley Cup Final debut as the Hurricanes look to shift momentum in the championship series. The game is scheduled for 6:00 p.m. at Vegas.

cards.headline: SoFi Stadium workers reach deal to avoid World Cup strike
cards.teaser: Food and beverage workers union announces tentative agreement days before World Cup matches begin.
cards.body:
Workers at SoFi Stadium have reached a tentative labor agreement, averting a planned strike ahead of the World Cup. The deal was announced Tuesday afternoon by the union representing cashiers, dishwashers, cooks, bartenders, and other food service and concessions workers.

The agreement prevents a work stoppage that would have disrupted World Cup matches at the Los Angeles venue. However, the union retained its contractual right to strike if federal immigration enforcement threatens worker safety during the tournament. The US opens play against Paraguay at SoFi Stadium on June 12.

cards.headline: Somali referee denied entry to United States for World Cup
cards.teaser: Omar Artan will miss the World Cup after being barred from entering the country.
cards.body:
Somali referee Omar Artan has been denied entry to the United States and will miss the 2026 World Cup. Artan would have made history as the first Somali official to referee at the tournament.

His case is part of a broader pattern affecting the 2026 World Cup, where FIFA's tournament has become entangled in the Trump administration's strict border restrictions. Multiple World Cup players and officials have reportedly been detained or barred from entering the United States ahead of the tournament, marking a significant departure from previous World Cups where host nations have typically granted easier entry for participants.

hero.headline: Jay-Z and Eminem to Collaborate on Rakim Album After 25 Years
hero.body:
Jay-Z and Eminem will reunite on a new Rakim album, marking their first collaboration in 25 years. The track appears on a collaborative album featuring Rakim, Kurupt, and Masta Killa.

The collaboration represents a significant moment in hip-hop, bringing together three generations of rap artists. Jay-Z and Eminem last worked together a quarter-century ago, and their reunion on this project pays tribute to Rakim, widely regarded as one of the most influential figures in rap history.

Rakim, who rose to prominence in the 1980s as part of the duo Eric B. & Rakim, revolutionized hip-hop with his complex rhyme schemes and introspective lyricism. His influence shaped the careers of countless artists who followed, including both Jay-Z and Eminem. The collaborative album also features Kurupt, known for his work with Tha Dogg Pound and Death Row Records, and Masta Killa of the Wu-Tang Clan.

The project brings together artists from different eras and coasts of hip-hop. Jay-Z, who built his career in New York before becoming a business mogul, and Eminem, who emerged from Detroit to become one of the best-selling artists of all time, have both cited Rakim as a foundational influence on their approaches to rapping. Their decision to collaborate on this album reflects the respect Rakim commands within the hip-hop community.

No release date for the album has been announced. The collaboration arrives at a time when legacy hip-hop artists have increasingly worked together on projects that celebrate the genre's history and evolution. Both Jay-Z and Eminem remain active in music, though both have reduced their recording output in recent years to focus on other ventures.

cards.headline: Zahara Jolie Files to Drop Pitt Last Name
cards.teaser: Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie's daughter Zahara has filed legal paperwork to remove her father's last name.
cards.body:
Zahara Jolie-Pitt has taken legal steps to formally remove Pitt from her last name. The filing represents the latest development in the ongoing estrangement between Brad Pitt and several of his children with Angelina Jolie.

Maddox, another of the couple's children, is expected to appear in court to explain why he wants his father's name removed. The legal actions come years after Jolie filed for divorce from Pitt in 2016, following an incident on a private plane that reportedly involved an altercation between Pitt and Maddox.

cards.headline: Chris Brown Settles Lawsuit Over Song Credits
cards.teaser: The singer resolved a legal dispute with a lyricist who accused him of denying credit and cutting them out of millions in revenue.
cards.body: Chris Brown has reached a settlement in a lawsuit filed by a lyricist over the songs Monalisa and Sensational. The plaintiff accused Brown of failing to provide proper credit and excluding them from significant revenue generated by the tracks. The lawsuit had alleged that Brown profited from the lyricist's contributions without appropriate compensation or recognition, potentially amounting to millions of dollars in lost revenue.

cards.headline: Nicholas Galitzine to Star in Hoyt Richards Biopic Directed by Gus Van Sant
cards.teaser: The actor will portray the model in a biographical film helmed by the acclaimed director.
cards.body:
Nicholas Galitzine has been cast as Hoyt Richards in a biographical film to be directed by Gus Van Sant. Richards was a prominent male model who later became known for his involvement with a religious cult.

Van Sant, whose directing credits include Good Will Hunting and Milk, will helm the project. Galitzine has recently appeared in films including Red, White & Royal Blue and The Idea of You, establishing himself as a rising actor in Hollywood.

cards.headline: Persimmon Acquires Mystery Film Death on the Brandywine
cards.teaser: The independent distributor secured U.S. and international rights to the film starring Kate Burton.
cards.body:
Persimmon has acquired distribution rights for Death on the Brandywine in the United States and several international territories. The mystery film stars Kate Burton, known for her role on Grey's Anatomy, along with Rena Sofer, Tuc Watkins, Jay Huguley, Walt Willey, Shanley Caswell, and Guy Nardulli.

The acquisition adds to Persimmon's catalog of independent films. The cast includes actors with extensive television credits, ranging from dramas like 24 and NCIS: New Orleans to daytime soap operas.

cards.headline: Sun Valley 2026 Media Summit Attendee List Revealed
cards.teaser: David Ellison, Bari Weiss, Josh D'Amaro, Jeff Bezos, and other media and tech leaders will attend the annual Idaho retreat.
cards.body:
Allen & Co. has announced the attendee roster for its 2026 Sun Valley conference, the annual gathering of media and technology executives held in Idaho. The confirmed guest list includes David Ellison, journalist Bari Weiss, Disney Parks chairman Josh D'Amaro, and Amazon founder Jeff Bezos.

The invitation-only event serves as a venue for major business deals and strategic discussions among industry leaders. The conference features panel discussions alongside informal networking opportunities throughout the summer gathering.

cards.headline: Adults Season 2 to Premiere in August on FX
cards.teaser: The entire eight-episode season will be released on FXX on-demand and Hulu on August 27.
cards.body:
FX has set an August 27 premiere date for the second season of Adults. All eight episodes will be available at once on FXX on-demand and Hulu starting at 9 p.m. Eastern time, with two episodes airing weekly on the FXX linear channel.

Guest stars for the season include Jake Shane and Gaten Matarazzo. The series will also be available internationally on Disney+.

hero.headline: U.S. launches strikes on Iranian air defenses after helicopter downing
hero.body:
President Trump directed U.S. Central Command to launch strikes against Iranian radar and air defense systems along the Strait of Hormuz beginning Tuesday evening, in response to Iran's downing of an American Apache helicopter. The military conducted multiple rounds of attacks targeting facilities in the strategic waterway.

The helicopter downing and subsequent U.S. retaliation mark a dangerous escalation in tensions between the two countries. This comes after a ceasefire announced in April, and follows Trump's February operations against Iranian leadership. Despite the military strikes, Trump indicated he believes a deal with Iran remains possible, maintaining his dual approach of military pressure combined with diplomatic outreach.

cards.headline: House passes pro-union bill after 20 Republicans break with leadership
cards.teaser: The Faster Labor Contracts Act sets shorter timelines for first-contract negotiations for newly formed unions.
cards.body:
The House passed the Faster Labor Contracts Act on Tuesday with support from 20 Republicans who broke ranks with party leadership. The bill shortens the timeline for first-contract negotiations when workers form new unions and allows government intervention if agreements aren't reached within 90 days.

This marks another instance of pro-labor House Republicans voting against their party's position on employment measures. The legislation represents a significant win for labor groups and populist lawmakers who have pushed for stronger worker protections in contract negotiations.

cards.headline: Justice Department finds EEOC hiring guidelines unconstitutional
cards.teaser: The Office of Legal Counsel opinion concludes the guidelines pressure employers to consider race in hiring decisions.
cards.body:
The Justice Department's Office of Legal Counsel issued an opinion on Tuesday declaring the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission's hiring guidelines unconstitutional. The opinion found the guidelines pressure employers to take race into consideration during the hiring process.

While the Office of Legal Counsel opinion does not carry the force of a court ruling, it could make it more difficult for employees to bring discrimination claims against employers. The finding represents a significant shift in how federal agencies approach workplace discrimination enforcement.

cards.headline: Trump administration warns 500 hospitals over missing price information
cards.teaser: Warning letters cite failures to comply with federal price transparency requirements for medical services.
cards.body:
The Trump administration issued warning letters to more than 500 hospitals nationwide for failing to comply with federal price transparency requirements. The hospitals have not disclosed costs of medical services as mandated by federal rules, according to the administration.

The administration argues that the lack of price transparency drives health care costs higher than necessary. The Associated Press obtained a list of the hundreds of hospitals that received the warnings, which could lead to fines if the facilities do not comply with the disclosure requirements.

cards.headline: Georgia Democrat renews push for federal red flag gun law
cards.teaser: Rep. Lucy McBath introduced legislation to expand red flag laws nationwide to address gun violence.
cards.body:
Rep. Lucy McBath (D-Ga.) renewed her push for federal red flag legislation on Tuesday at a press conference on Capitol Hill. McBath promoted her Federal Extreme Risk Protection Order Act as a measure designed to save lives by allowing temporary firearm removal from individuals deemed dangerous.

McBath's son, Jordan Davis, was fatally shot at a Florida gas station. The congresswoman has made gun violence prevention a central focus of her legislative work since joining Congress.

cards.headline: Meta accuses Israeli spyware firm of violating court order on WhatsApp
cards.teaser: The technology company asked a federal court to hold NSO Group in contempt for alleged phishing attempts.
cards.body:
Meta accused Israeli spyware firm NSO Group of violating a US court order by targeting WhatsApp users with malicious links. The company said it caught and disrupted spear phishing attempts by NSO Group directed at a handful of users in Jordan and Lebanon.

Meta also discovered that NSO Group had created test accounts and groups on WhatsApp. The allegations suggest the spyware firm continued its surveillance activities despite existing court restrictions on such operations.

cards.headline: Maine and South Carolina hold primaries as House passes reconciliation bill
cards.teaser: Progressive oyster farmer Graham Platner will face Sen. Susan Collins after winning the Democratic primary.
cards.body:
The House passed a $70 billion bill on Tuesday to fund immigration enforcement through the remainder of Trump's term, ending a four-month lapse in funding for the Department of Homeland Security and ICE. Democrats have criticized the legislation, arguing Congress has ceded its oversight role to the administration's immigration agenda.

In other House action, the Faster Labor Contracts Act passed with bipartisan support, including 20 Republicans crossing party lines to join Democrats. The bill imposes shorter timelines for first-contract negotiations for newly formed unions, marking a significant victory for labor groups and populist lawmakers.
